h01: Pumps not updated in shift()/sync() → oracle manipulation

lessons.detail: 53 people submitted HIGH, only 1 unique bug accepted (H-01). The rest were duplicates or wrong. Competition is BRUTAL.
lessons.action: Speed matters. First to submit gets primary credit.

lessons.detail: skim() "access control" (6 dups) — by design, permissionless. shift() "front-running" (5 dups) — MEV, not a bug. fee-on-transfer (5 dups) — out of scope. These are FALSE POSITIVES that many auditors fall for.
lessons.action: Before submitting: Is this BY DESIGN? Is this MEV? Is this IN SCOPE?

lessons.detail: H-01: shift() and sync() skip _updatePumps(). Not a reentrancy, not an overflow, not access control. It was a MISSING FUNCTION CALL in an alternative code path. The kind of bug that pattern matching CANNOT find.
lessons.action: For every state-updating function: check ALL entry points call the same update functions. Map: entry point → side effects.

lessons.detail: Many "low quality report" rejections. Reports without PoC, without clear impact, without code references → rejected. Even valid bugs get rejected if poorly written.
lessons.action: Every submission needs: (1) exact line numbers, (2) clear impact statement, (3) PoC or attack flow, (4) why this is NOT by design.

lessons.detail: Many findings were technically correct but not exploitable. E.g., "anyone can call skim()" — true, but skim only takes excess tokens not in reserves. No fund loss.
lessons.action: Always calculate: Can attacker PROFIT? If not, its not HIGH.
